what: A frame holding text stays pinned to the screen, and from inside the frame a white fill spreads to a brush-stroke edge and covers the whole stage while the frame grows past the screen — a door from a dark world into a white paper world inside the picture. In one scroll-bound timeline the words of the text fade out one by one starting at .12, and the fill spreads from .26 for .64 with power2.in (radius = progress × panel diagonal / .55), and the frame grows from .34 for .6 with power1.inOut by (panel-covering ratio × 1.04)^progress. The paint edge is a WebGL shader: it reaches as far as the distance around the frame plus directional noise blobs (.55 + .75 times), brush grain and bristle marks, dry brush tips split by strand noise, and 7% dark tone mixed into the outer 18px of the edge. When the paint passes the top of the frame, the panel gets data-tone="light"

options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Panel attached to the screen — the paint canvas lies beneath it
options.[data-fx-part=frame]: Frame that will grow (fill starts inside the border thickness)
options.[data-fx-part=text]: Text whose words blur out one by one (optional)
options.[data-fx-part=label]: Hint that fades near the end (optional)

use: Your text here
